owner: Hypercurve qualification tooling and public fixture catalog (planM0, propertiesP37/P39 plus P12-P20 stage claims).
missing_witness: No executable cross-stage capability catalog found by rg. FUTURE_WORK currently keeps manually maintained scoped matrices. Existing public tests cover exact success and typed polynomial blockers but are not assembled into a current revision-pinned matrix.
proposed_after_native_pair_commit: Use a small declarative fixture catalog with explicit domains, native/generated families, owning layers, per-stage claims and asserted outcome. Keep target coverage separate from demonstrated fixture coverage.
Reuse reviewed existing public integration tests and focused owner regressions. A passing unsupported-frontier assertion must remain a recorded implementation gap, not exact completion.

Runner builds selected targets with locked release/all-features settings, locates exact registered tests, invokes one named fixture in a fresh process, and rejects zero-test success, ignored-without-opt-in, nonzero exit, assertion failure and external timeout. Record builds separately from completed fixture cost.

Keep raw JSON/logs under ignored target or an explicit evidence destination, record source revision/dirty patch, compiler, feature policy, binary digests and source stability, and archive only qualification evidence later.
A timeout is external/incomplete, not typed resource exhaustion. Existing WorkBudget tests prove counted refinement/promotion exhaustion and retry only.
Meaningful Python tests should reject malformed catalogs, unknown tests, zero-test matches and failed/timeout runs. Geometry fixtures remain unchanged unless a missing public witness is added.

No universal closure or fresh-process native replay claim follows from a catalog. Same-process authored SVG tests qualify only their authored tags and existing assertions; generated replay remains a separate gap.
